claim: LM-PACE estimates GPT-4 confidence for cloud-incident root-cause generation on 121,308 internal Microsoft incidents and evaluates it with ECE and reliability diagrams only; labels are GPT-4 pseudo-labels (similarity >= 2.3)
uncertainty: Split sizes (98,308 / 2,000 / 3,000) do not sum to the stated total; FSE version not read; data private
decision_relevance: Closest in-domain prior: LLM-RCA confidence is not new. H1 must claim selective risk at matched coverage under controlled telemetry removal on public fault-injection labels, none of which LM-PACE has

claim: With low confidence-of-evaluation (little historical evidence) the model tends to overestimate incorrect root causes
uncertainty: Qualitative distribution reading, not a controlled ablation
decision_relevance: Supports the H1 premise that scarce evidence produces confidently wrong RCA outputs

claim: AutoCrashFL confidence (max suspiciousness over R runs) correlates weakly with correctness (point-biserial 0.23 vs 0.57 in AutoFL); Brier 0.357 is worse than the naive 0.25 and Platt scaling brings it to 0.199
uncertainty: Crash-stack localisation at SAP HANA, not service-level RCA; single industrial system
decision_relevance: Raw LLM-derived confidence is poorly calibrated in software fault localisation; recalibration fitted on DEV is required before any abstention claim (protocol v2 already allows DEV-fit rules)

claim: TelemetrySuffBench masks seven telemetry factors on agent traces and tests safe abstention: evidence gating cuts unsupported unique-origin answers by 12.5-48.6 pp for three of five frontier models, while two models still answer every ambiguous case
uncertainty: Synthetic delayed-binding faults in LLM-agent workflows, not microservice incidents; anonymous artifact
decision_relevance: Closest design neighbour of H1 (telemetry masking + abstention + frontier LLMs). Narrows H1 novelty to microservice RCA with fault-injection ground truth and matched-coverage selective risk

pub_status: preprint (arXiv, 2 Oct 2026); dataset and models on Hugging Face
claim: Nautil (731 cases incl. production server incidents) tests evidence dependence by removing a conclusion's grounds: closure falls 26 points for the fine-tuned 9B model but only 6 (base) and 7 (frontier) points; a frontier model with 84% correct causes overstates in 91% of answers and closes 17 of 41 'cause undetermined' cases
uncertainty: Mostly accident reports; host incidents lack ground-truth root causes; judged with LLM judges
decision_relevance: Counterfactual evidence removal + abstention already exists outside microservice RCA; also shows prompting alone barely reacts to removed evidence, which supports measuring H1 with a deterministic rule rather than model self-abstention

claim: Host (server-incident) labels do not reproduce: re-investigating, a frontier model closed only 5 of 39 host cases labelled should-close
uncertainty: Appendix result on 39 cases
decision_relevance: Incident labels from operator closure markers are unreliable; NT114's fault-injection labels are a methodological advantage worth stating

claim: CoreSec replaces weighted score fusion with a PAM-style abstention algebra for datacenter-network RCA, giving deterministic decisions and explicit abstention when evidence is ambiguous
uncertainty: Experience paper; no public data or selective-risk numbers located
decision_relevance: Abstention for RCA under partial telemetry is deployed practice (non-LLM, rule-based); H1 cannot claim abstention in RCA as new, only its measured effect for LLMs

claim: CROC builds finite-sample valid conformal confidence sets for the root-cause index in multi-stream data, assuming independent streams and exchangeable pre/post-change samples
uncertainty: Statistical change-point setting, not LLM, not microservice benchmarks
decision_relevance: A distribution-free set-valued alternative to thresholded abstention exists for RCA; usable as a related-work contrast and possibly as a non-LLM set baseline

claim: Of 58 SR1-extracted papers whose title is RCA / fault localisation / incident, 0 report selective prediction at matched coverage ('yes'), 4 report it partially, 42 have no confidence source, 16 use controlled modality removal, and only 3 combine controlled removal with any confidence signal (AutoCrashFL, Eadro, TVDiag; none LLM-verbal or consensus)
evidence_location: work/raw/sr1/extract.csv (title regex in the report, section 3)

decision_relevance: Supports that the exact H1 cell (LLM confidence x controlled telemetry removal x matched-coverage risk on RCA benchmarks) is unfilled in the reviewed corpus

claim: ARMOR targets RCA under missing modality and argues unified multimodal frameworks unrealistically assume complete data; evaluated on two datasets (D1, D2)

claim: PORCA formulates root cause analysis with partially observed data, addressing unobserved confounders and heterogeneity

claim: ReconRCA performs microservice RCA with incomplete metrics

claim: Studies LLM abstention in science QA when the context is perturbed, including removal of gold context

uncertainty: Abstract-level; QA, not RCA

claim: Early models often avoid questions, whereas scaled-up, shaped-up models more often give an apparently sensible but wrong answer

claim: Reasoning models often detect that a problem is under-specified yet still produce an unsupported final answer (detection-to-abstention gap)
uncertainty: Missing-premise math/medical QA

claim: LLM uncertainty estimators that work without ambiguity degrade to close-to-random performance on ambiguous QA data

claim: Cross-model disagreement is proposed as a label-free correctness signal for confident errors
uncertainty: QA tasks

claim: For code predictions, post-hoc calibration reduces probability misalignment but does not improve discrimination between correct and incorrect outputs
uncertainty: Code tasks
decision_relevance: Recalibration (Platt) will not by itself improve AURC; H1's gain must come from a discriminative signal

claim: JustDiag adds calibrated non-closure to RCA: on 66 proprietary incidents the outcome score rises 51.0 -> 57.7 while completion falls 65/66 -> 62/66
uncertainty: 66 private incidents; no CIs located

claim: Over 40 standard-tier adversarial IR episodes per model, GPT-5.2 executes containment in 100% of episodes with an 82.5% false-positive rate, acting at step 4 before gathering sufficient evidence

claim: Across nine causal-discovery and 21 RCA methods, no method stands out in all situations

claim: BudgetSRE treats tokens, tool calls and action depth as a budget, invoking a specialist agent only under high diagnostic uncertainty; on AIOpsLab it stays within 4-6 pp of an unconstrained oracle at medium budget

claim: With the actual E1 estimator, injection clustering, 11-level consensus ties and percentile cluster bootstrap, the fixed-coverage (0.7) gain MDE at 80% power is about 0.05-0.06 on RCAEval full and the pooled single-modality set, 0.05 on AIOps2025 and 0.08-0.10 on Nezha / RCA100 (alpha 0.05), under a binomial-logit generator
